chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Umar ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Beware of divorcing three women in one sitting, for they are those who have husbands.

key_terms.ذَوَاتُ الْأَزْوَاجِ: Those who have husbands (indicating they remain married)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorcing three wives at once in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia jurisprudential view on *talqat thalath* (three divorces in one sitting), asserting that all three are counted simultaneously, rendering the wife fully divorced but requiring a *halala* marriage before she can remarry her original husband. This ruling contrasts with some Sunni schools that may count them sequentially, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the immediate legal effect of the utterance. The warning underscores the gravity of treating divorce as a casual act rather than a solemn legal procedure.
